items.title: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy
items.text: Date: 2026-07-16 Author: Codebot Topic: homelab, LiteLLM, Caddy, SSL, NixOS, sudo
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Import homelab CA certificate to Windows Trusted Root Store to resolve browser "connection not secure" error for litellm.home.arpa.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Browser showed "your connection isn't secure" for litellm.home.arpa. CA cert available at /mnt/homelab/home/homelab-ca.crt. Simple certutil import expected to resolve.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: After CA import, browser error changed to ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID. Certificate trusted but hostname mismatch. Server cert generated before litellm.home.arpa added to Caddyfile. Wildcard DNS:*.home.arpa should match but Chrome treats .arpa as public suffix, blocking wildcard matches. Only explicit SAN entries work.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.1 CA Certificate Import
items.text:
• Copied cert to Windows Desktop
  • Ran certutil -addstore -f Root
  • UAC prompt accepted
  • Cert landed in Trusted Root Store
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.2 Hostname Mismatch Diagnosis
items.text:
• Traced through NixOS stack: homelab.crt generated by homelab-cert oneshot service
  • SANs built from Caddy service list
  • litellm.home.arpa in Caddyfile but cert generated before addition
  • Wildcard DNS:*.home.arpa present but Chrome blocks .arpa wildcard matches
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.3 Certificate Regeneration Requirement
items.text:
• Fix: sudo systemctl restart homelab-cert.service && sudo systemctl restart Caddy
  • Blocked: agent cannot sudo (password required, no interactive SSH)
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.4 Sudo Policy Design
items.text:
• Drafted sudo.nix module using security.sudo.extraRules
  • First attempt: rule order wrong (NOPASSWD ALL last, overriding nixos-rebuild restriction)
  • Sudoers rule: last matching rule's tags win
  • Fixed order: NOPASSWD ALL first, PASSWD nixos-rebuild last
  • Rebuild confirmed: sudo -n whoami returns root, sudo -n nixos-rebuild requires password
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 4.5 Certificate Regeneration
items.text:
• With sudo working, restarted homelab-cert.service and Caddy
  • New cert includes litellm.home.arpa in explicit SANs
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Chrome public suffix list treats .arpa as TLD equivalent, disabling wildcard SAN matching. Cert generation timing (before Caddyfile update) caused missing SAN. Sudo policy required for operational automation without compromising generation safety.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: CA cert trusted on Windows. Server cert regenerated with explicit litellm.home.arpa SAN. Sudo policy: NOPASSWD for operations, PASSWD for nixos-rebuild. All from single cert import request.
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Imported homelab CA to Windows Trusted Root Store
  • Diagnosed .arpa wildcard blocking by Chrome public suffix rules
  • Designed sudo.nix with correct rule ordering (NOPASSWD first, PASSWD nixos-rebuild last)
  • Regenerated server cert with explicit litellm.home.arpa SAN
  • Verified sudo -n works for operations, blocks nixos-rebuild
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Verify browser access to litellm.home.arpa shows secure
  • Test sudo -n for operational commands
  • Confirm sudo -n nixos-rebuild requires password
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Monitor cert renewal automation
  • Document .arpa public suffix behavior for future certs
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Add hostnames to Caddyfile before cert generation
  • Use explicit SANs for .arpa domains (no wildcards)
  • Order sudo rules: permissive first, restrictive last
  • Separate operational sudo from generation sudo
path: The Cert That Led To A Sudo Policy

items.title: The LiteLLM Gateway Evolution - Part 1
items.text:
Podman migration & stabilization

Date: 2026-07-19 Author: Codebot Topic: homelab, LiteLLM, Podman, NixOS, Caddy, troubleshooting

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Stabilize LiteLLM proxy on NixOS homelab through Podman container migration, auto-restart system, and configuration fixes over three days (9 sessions).

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: LiteLLM migrated from systemd-native service to Podman container fronted by Caddy on port 4000. Two profiles shared hardware: #homelab (headless) and #workstation (desktop GUI). Operational wrapper handled config rendering, provider management, CLI tools. Proxy unreachable initially.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Container crash-looping, config mount path mismatch between image versions, rogue provider in runtime models.json, 502 errors from Caddy, database requirements for UI, sudo policy conflicts, wall command freezing terminals, profile targeting confusion.

items.title: 4.1 Day 1: Initial Access and Config Changes
items.text:
• SSH into homelab, navigated to /srv/repo/nix-lab/modules/ai/
  • Modified wrapper: litellm-render auto-restart via systemd path unit
  • Added file watching for config.yaml
  • Committed, rebuilt, tested

items.title: 4.2 Day 1 Evening: Container Crash-Loop Fix
items.text:
• Root cause 1: :main tag entrypoint reads /app/proxy_server_config.yaml, but Nix module mounted to /app/config.yaml. LiteLLM fell back to bundled Azure config and crashed.
  • Root cause 2: :main nightly hangs on large configs (131 models). Switched to v1.92.0 stable.
  • Version-specific mount path: v1.92.0 reads /app/config.yaml (correct), :main reads /app/proxy_server_config.yaml.
  • Fixed: pinned v1.92.0, mounted to correct path.
  • Removed rogue mygpu provider from runtime models.json (no API key).

items.title: 4.3 Day 2: Provenance Tracking and No-Rebuild Provider
items.text:
• Item 2: litellm-add-provider supports --models '' for single-step provider+model registration. Each model gets origin.type=manual, added_at timestamp.
  • Item 3: Added origin provenance metadata to models.json, threaded through renderer to config.yaml. Every model carries source (declared vs discovered vs manual). Merge logic preserves manual-origin across rebuilds.

items.title: 4.4 Day 2 Evening: 502 Debug and Constraints
items.text:
• 502 from Caddy: container up but refusing connections.
  • LiteLLM v1.92.0 expects database for UI login. Rendered config had no database_url.
  • Tried SQLite database_url: crash-loop. SQLite support broken in v1.92.0 image.
  • Reverted to no-DB mode: proxy works, UI login non-functional (accepted).
  • Three constraints documented in AGENTS.md:
  • wall broadcasts freeze terminals -> reverted to logger only
  • Sudo policy: passwordless for all except nixos-rebuild (prevent accidental generation changes) -> locked down

items.title: homelab vs #workstation on same hardware -> always rebuild workstation
4.5 Day 3: Cleanup and Documentation
items.text:
• Removed duplicate cmd in Nix module (entrypoint ignores it)
  • Added logs/ volume mount (harmless, journald primary)
  • Updated README: pinned image, config mount path, no-DB limitation
  • Certificate never the problem: Caddy serves valid *.home.arpa from Homelab Internal CA. Browser errors were client-side trust.

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Image version dictates config mount path. Large configs hang on nightly. Database required for UI but SQLite broken in v1.92.0. Operational constraints (sudo, wall, profile targeting) must be codified. Client-side cert trust != server cert validity.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Stable LiteLLM container on v1.92.0 behind Caddy. Auto-restart on config changes. No-rebuild provider registration. Provenance tracking through pipeline. Locked-down sudo policy. AGENTS.md documents operational knowledge.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Pinned LiteLLM to v1.92.0 with correct config mount (/app/config.yaml)
  • Implemented systemd path unit auto-restart on config.yaml changes
  • Added no-rebuild provider registration with provenance metadata
  • Accepted no-DB mode (UI login non-functional, API proxy works)
  • Codified 3 operational constraints in AGENTS.md
  • Documented pinned image, mount path, limitations in README

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Verify container stability over time
  • Test auto-restart on provider/model changes
  • Confirm no-rebuild provider registration works
  • Validate sudo policy enforcement

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Rename litellm/ to gateway/ (deferred)
  • Daily fetch-models timer under wrapper (deferred)

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Pin container images to stable versions
  • Match config mount path to image version expectations
  • Accept UI limitations when database backend problematic
  • Document operational constraints in AGENTS.md
  • Always target workstation profile on shared hardware

items.title: Coding with Hermes Agent - Part 1
items.text:
Building a Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestrator and running the first cycle

Date: 2026-07-18 Author: Codebot Topic: Hermes Agent, OpenCode, workflow, orchestrator, Electron, project-management

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Establish automated multi-agent workflow between Hermes Agent (strategist/reviewer) and OpenCode (coder) with human as project manager, using structured state-machine orchestration.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: User wanted Hermes Agent and OpenCode to collaborate in automated loop. Initial ad-hoc relay (terminal OpenCode run) worked for single prompts but not multi-turn. Explored three communication modes before settling on artifact-driven state machine.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Simple turn-taking doesn't scale to multiple specialized agents. Need structured workflow with human-in-the-loop gates, persistent artifacts, and clear authority boundaries.

items.title: 4.1 Communication Mode Exploration
items.text: Mode Description Result 1. Ad-hoc relay opencode run as one-shot subprocess Works for single prompts, slow for multi-turn (cold start) 2. Long-lived server opencode serve HTTP API (port 4096, SSE, OpenAPI 3.1) Security issue: /config/providers returns all API keys plaintext even with Basic Auth. Mitigation: bind localhost, strong password. 3. Autonomous loop Python converse.py alternating Hermes Agent chat / opencode run Proved functional: 6 sec/turn with free tier (opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free). Google models timeout via OpenCode but work via Hermes.

items.title: 4.2 State Machine Redesign
items.text:
User rejected alternation model. Designed workflow state machine:

  • Roles: Project Manager (human), Code Reviewer (Hermes Agent), Coder (OpenCode)
  • Artifacts: status.json, objective.md, plan.md, implementation.diff, review.md, decision.md, coder-reply.md, workspace/, README.md, transcript.md
  • States: CLARIFY -> PLAN -> AUTHORIZE -> IMPLEMENT -> REVIEW -> APPROVED -> COMPLETE
  • Authority: OpenCode never receives task without explicit PM authorization. Control returns to human between agent actions.

items.title: 4.3 Orchestrator Implementation
items.text:
workflow.py CLI with step-advance pattern:

python3 workflow.py --init session/todoist-wrapper --objective "Create Electron app for Todoist"
python3 workflow.py --advance session/todoist-wrapper  # -> PLAN
python3 workflow.py --approve session/todoist-wrapper  # -> IMPLEMENT
python3 workflow.py --advance session/todoist-wrapper  # -> REVIEW

Coder step: opencode run returns conversational text. Script extracts markdown code blocks with filenames, writes to workspace/. Cleaning functions strip Hermes Agent CLI overhead and OpenCode ANSI/headers.

items.title: 4.4 First Cycle: Todoist Electron Wrapper
items.text:
Objective: Minimal Electron wrapper for Todoist.com (1200x800, frameless, custom title bar, UA spoofing).

Successes:

  • Thorough plan: security (contextBridge, no nodeIntegration), error handling, UA spoofing
  • Clean code: main.js, preload.js (draggable title bar overlay), package.json (Electron v33)
  • Full cycle ~8 minutes, zero manual intervention post-approval
  • Git initialized at session root (artifacts) and workspace/ (code diffs)

Failures Fixed:

  • Deep nesting: OpenCode prefixed workspace/ -> workspace/workspace/main.js. Fixed by stripping prefixes.
  • Verdict parsing: instruction examples (VERDICT: APPROVED) leaked into output. Fixed by filtering instruction lines.
  • Stray node_modules: 271MB under skill scripts from test run.
  • Session state sync: do_approve saved AUTHORIZE before IMPLEMENT. If OpenCode hung, state stuck. Fixed by deferring save.

items.title: 4.5 Code Quality Standards (Reviewer Prompt)
items.text: 8-point standard: descriptive names, error handling required, no hardcoded secrets, input safety, demo boundary, cross-platform fallbacks, well-known dependencies, comments on non-obvious logic.

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Opencode run is conversational, not file-writing - requires markdown block extraction. Google models route poorly through OpenCode (timeouts) but work via Hermes. Free tier (opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free) responds in 6-10 sec. State machines scale better than turn-taking for 3+ agents. Artifact cleaning critical - prompt instructions leak into output.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Orchestrator functional with crash-safe state machine. First cycle produced working Electron app. Artifact-driven approach provides complete audit trail.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Designed 3-role, 7-state workflow with artifact gates
  • Implemented workflow.py with step-advance CLI
  • Extracted code from conversational OpenCode output via markdown blocks
  • Completed first cycle: Todoist Electron wrapper (COMPLETE with decision.md override)
  • Documented 8-point code quality standard
  • Skill at ~/.hermes/skills/software-development/project-manager-assistant/ (v0.3)

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Test recovery from OpenCode timeout
  • Add knowledge/RAG agent
  • Fix stray scripts/workspace/ directory

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Fix scripts/workspace/ stray directory cleanup
  • Add error recovery for OpenCode timeout
  • Make --advance for AUTHORIZE flow automatically into IMPLEMENT
  • Add knowledge/RAG agent

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Use OpenCode free tier for programmatic calls (reliable, fast)
  • Avoid Google models via OpenCode (routing timeouts)
  • Aggressively strip prompt instructions from agent outputs
  • State machine > turn-taking for multi-agent workflows
  • Artifact-driven design enables audit and recovery

Todoist wrapper: prototype vs workflow build

Date: 2026-07-18 Author: Codebot Topic: Electron, todoist, prototyping, pm-assistant, workflow

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Build desktop wrapper for Todoist.com (1200x800, frameless, custom icon) and compare standalone prototype vs PM Assistant workflow-driven build.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Simple Electron app request. Two approaches tested in 15 minutes: direct code generation vs structured PM Assistant workflow.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Need to evaluate whether workflow overhead provides value for simple projects.

items.title: 4.1 Standalone Prototype
items.text:
• Direct code request
  • Result: minimal project in /home/sigit/workspace/
  • Files: main.js (loads URL), preload.js (stub), 256x256 red rounded-square icon (pure Python)
  • Run: npm start -> frameless, exit via Alt+F4

items.title: 4.2 PM Assistant Build
items.text:
• Same objective through PM Assistant workflow
  • Reviewer wrote 7-step plan first
  • Coder built to plan
  • Result: polished implementation
  • Custom Chrome 120 User-Agent (avoids Todoist anti-bot blocking)
  • Preload injects semi-transparent draggable title bar with close button (backdrop-filter: blur)
  • 512x512 icon with white "T" on red background (pure Python)

items.title: 4.3 Comparison
items.text: Aspect Standalone PM Assistant Speed Faster Few minutes more UA Spoofing Missing Included Window Controls Alt+F4 only Draggable title bar + close button Icon 256x256 red square 512x512 styled "T" Preload Skeleton Functional with IPC Planning None 7-step plan caught edge cases

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Planning step forced consideration of "what does frameless mean for daily use?" - caught Todoist UA blocking and missing window controls. Standalone build shipped but was incomplete for real use.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: PM Assistant build accepted as canonical. Both sessions cleaned up. Workflow-driven approach worth extra time for production use.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:

  • Standalone: minimal, fast, incomplete
  • PM Assistant: planned, polished, complete
  • Accepted PM Assistant version as canonical

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:

  • Verify UA spoofing prevents Todoist blocking
  • Confirm frameless UX with title bar controls

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: • None

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• For disposable prototypes: standalone approach acceptable
  • For daily-use tools: workflow-driven build worth overhead
  • Planning step catches real-world edge cases (UA blocking, UX gaps)
  • Frameless requires explicit window controls, not just Alt+F4

items.title: Coding with Hermes Agent - Part 3
items.text:
PM Assistant v0.4 — Crash-Safe and Configurable

Date: 2026-07-20 Author: Codebot Topic: Hermes Agent, pm-assistant, orchestration, recovery, retrospective

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Upgrade project-manager-assistant skill to v0.4 with crash-safe recovery, configurable agent roster, and automatic retrospect reporting.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: v0.3 was fragile: OpenCode crash left session corrupt (traceback on stdout, status.json possibly unwritten, half-written workspace files). Models hardcoded in workflow.py. No automatic project closure report.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Three fragility points: (1) no error recovery - crash = manual cleanup, (2) hardcoded models - no cheap swap when provider overloaded, (3) no project closure artifact - learning lost.

items.title: 4.1 Failure Recovery
items.text:
• Added try/except wrapper around action dispatch in main()
  • On any exception: write failure.md (error, traceback tail, recovery command), pin state to STUCK in status.json
  • --advance detects STUCK, prints recovery hint instead of crashing
  • --recover command re-runs failing state with clean workspace:
  • IMPLEMENT: wipes workspace/ (shutil.rmtree), re-inits git, calls coder fresh
  • CLARIFY/REVIEW: re-calls reviewer with same inputs
  • Other states: prints "nothing to recover"
  • No auto-retry, no state rewind - deliberate single-command recovery for "one project a day" workflow

items.title: 4.2 Agent Roster Configuration
items.text:
• Created agents.yaml at skill root with two slots: reviewer, coder
  • Each defines: command template ({prompt}, {model} placeholders), default_model, optional extra_args
  • Zero-dependency: ~30-line fallback parser for flat key:value format (uses PyYAML if available, silent fallback)
  • Per-session override: drop agents.yaml in session directory for project-specific models
  • Example: swap coder to google/gemini-2.5-pro for one project, keep opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free for others

items.title: 4.3 Retrospect Report
items.text:
• On COMPLETE entry, workflow.py writes retrospect.md automatically (templated, no LLM cost)
  • Time-per-state table from status.json history timestamps
  • Optional --retrospect --llm calls reviewer for "Lessons learned" paragraph
  • Rest of report templated

items.title: 4.4 README.md Quick Reference
items.text:
• Every --status prints quirks doc path
  • Human-scannable 6-section reference: CLI quick-ref, mental model, recovery flow, agents.yaml gotchas, retrospect caveats, session directory anatomy
  • Complements 350-line SKILL.md (model-facing)

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: try/except boundary (15 lines) transformed error UX from "read code" to "run --recover". Zero-dependency YAML parser worth 30 lines for skill portability. Mental model documentation (three verbs: --advance, --approve/--reject, --recover) was hardest but most valuable.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: v0.4 crash-safe, model-swappable, generates retrospect. Features deferred to v0.5: parallel sub-tasks, cross-project dependencies, configurable state-time CLI flag.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Added crash recovery: failure.md + STUCK state + --recover command
  • Added agents.yaml with zero-dependency parser and per-session override
  • Added automatic retrospect.md on COMPLETE (templated + optional LLM analysis)
  • Added human-readable README.md referenced by --status
  • v0.4 feature complete for "one project a day, crash Tuesday, recover Wednesday"

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Test --recover on simulated IMPLEMENT crash
  • Verify agents.yaml override in session directory
  • Check retrospect.md generation on COMPLETE
  • Confirm --status prints quirks path

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: • v0.5 features when requested: parallel sub-tasks, cross-project dependencies, state-time CLI flag

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Minimal try/except wrapper transforms error UX dramatically
  • Zero-dependency config parsing enables skill portability
  • Document mental model (verbs) explicitly for user adoption
  • Separate human-readable docs (README) from model-facing docs (SKILL.md)

items.title: The LiteLLM Gateway Evolution - Part 2
items.text:
Refactoring the LiteLLM Gateway: from a Four-Way Split to Inventory/Policy

Date: 2026-07-20 Author: Codebot Topic: LiteLLM, NixOS, homelab, architecture, OpenCode, controller-pattern

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Refactor LiteLLM gateway from four-way provider split to clean inventory/policy architecture with pure-join renderer.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: By 2026-07-17, gateway split into controller (pkgs/litellm-controller/, mkGateway entry point) and thin NixOS module (modules/ai/litellm/). Pipeline: models-dev.json -> litellm-render -> config.yaml -> LiteLLM service. Provider model had four independent lists with no shared truth source.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text:
Four independent provider lists answering different questions:

  • providers-open.nix: active backends (auto from models-dev.json)
  • providers-restricted.nix: blocklist (no credits, paid-only, free-requiring-topup)
  • providers-manual.nix: hand-added (Gemini, Ollama)
  • lib/health.nix: separate registry with env vars and health endpoints

Adding provider required editing four files. Renderer had fallback tables and classification logic baked in. Health check carried own provider rules. Structural problem deferred from 2026-07-17 review.

items.title: 4.1 Redesign (2026-07-18)
items.text:
Separated questions into three files:

  • models.json: "What models exist?" Canonical inventory (discovered from models.dev + declared in declared-models.json). No secrets.
  • providers.json: "Which providers exposed and how?" Carries enabled, connection (api_base, api_key_env as name, prefix), endpoints (discovery path), policy (priority, disabled_models). No discovery metadata.
  • config.yaml: "How does LiteLLM implement policy?" Fully derived, never hand-edited.

items.title: 4.2 Pure-Join Renderer
items.text: Renderer became pure join: for each enabled provider, take inventory models, drop disabled_models, emit one YAML entry per model. No classification, fallback tables, or provider-specific if. Backend-agnostic - swapping LiteLLM only touches renderer.

items.title: 4.3 Legacy Removal
items.text: Deleted four-way Nix split: providers-open/-restricted/-manual.nix, health registry, providers-enabled.json, provider-defaults.json. Health check (litellm-doctor) now derives from providers.json (zero provider-specific rules).

items.title: 4.4 Runtime Editability
items.text: Committed providers-seed.json seeds runtime providers.json only on first boot (if absent). Runtime edits survive rebuild. litellm-add-provider as no-rebuild CLI.

items.title: 4.5 Key Fixes in Seed
items.text:
• aihubmix -> disabled (free requires topup)
  • fireworks-ai -> enabled (genuinely free)
  • Result: 131 models rendered with correct prefixes, litellm-doctor clean

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Four lists with same data = three too many. Drift inevitable. Collapsing to providers.json (policy+connection+endpoints) updates all consumers at once. Pure-join renderer discipline enables backend-agnostic data files. Runtime state editable without rebuild via seed-on-first-boot pattern.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Architecture quiet. 131 models rendered correctly. Doctor passes. Inventory/policy shape unchanged through later Podman transition and live backend tests.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Replaced 4 provider lists with 2 data files (models.json, providers.json) + derived config.yaml
  • Renderer: pure join (no provider logic)
  • Health check derives from providers.json
  • Runtime providers.json seeded once, editable without rebuild
  • No-rebuild CLI for provider additions
  • Fixed aihubmix/fireworks-ai classification in seed

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Verify litellm-doctor passes
  • Confirm 131 models rendered with correct prefixes
  • Test no-rebuild provider addition
  • Validate runtime edits survive rebuild

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Rename litellm/ to gateway/ (deferred)
  • Daily fetch-models timer (deferred)

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Single source of truth per question (inventory vs policy vs implementation)
  • Pure-join renderer worth upfront discipline
  • Seed runtime state on first boot only
  • Keep Nix build vs runtime state boundary explicit
  • Defer premature renames/timers

items.title: Experimenting with Hermes Agent - Part 7
items.text:
Overengineering a Hello World

Date: 2026-07-21 Author: Codebot Topic: Python, cli, prototyping, iteration, scope-creep

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Create a hello world CLI in Python with optional --name flag.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Simple request that should have completed in one session. Instead, five sessions over-engineered the solution through scope creep.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Iterative runs expanded structure without improving functionality. Each session produced working code but added unnecessary complexity.

items.title: 4.1 Session 1: Minimal Solution
items.text:
• Single hello.py with argparse
  • Shebang, executable
  • Works, complete

items.title: 4.2 Session 2: Package Structure
items.text:
• app/main.py with pyproject.toml
  • Console script entry point
  • pip install -e . support

items.title: 4.3 Session 3: Full Package Layout
items.text:
• hello-cli/ package
  • hello_cli/init.py and hello_cli/main.py
  • Three files for one-line program

items.title: 4.4 Session 4: Reset
items.text:
• Back to single hello.py
  • Implicit cycle acknowledgment

items.title: 4.5 Session 5: Code Review
items.text:
• Reviewed final implementation against objective
  • Objective: "hello world CLI app" - all versions satisfied
  • Nothing to fix; review was formality

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Testing workflow, not improving hello world. Trying different project structures, watching PM Assistant scaffold. Hello world was vehicle, not target. More runs != more progress.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Five sessions, same functional result. First answer was correct. Scope creep disguised as exploration.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Session 1: hello.py (argparse) - correct and complete
  • Sessions 2-4: progressive over-engineering (package, full layout, reset)
  • Session 5: review confirmed all versions met objective

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Verify hello.py --name works
  • Confirm no functional difference between versions

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: • None

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Accept first working solution for simple tasks
  • Distinguish workflow testing from feature development
  • Scope creep often disguises as "exploration"
  • More iterations do not guarantee better outcomes

items.title: Experimenting with Hermes Agent - Part 8
items.text:
PM Assistant Builds a Text Editor: First Real Workload

Date: 2026-07-21 Author: Codebot Topic: pm-assistant, multi-agent, text-editor, web, session-management

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Execute first real workload through PM Assistant skill: build browser-based text editor (single HTML file, no build tools) with file load/edit/save, syntax highlighting (3+ languages), line numbers, dark theme.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: PM Assistant v0.4 workflow with state machine: INIT -> PLANNING -> PLAN_REVIEW -> IMPLEMENTING -> VERIFYING -> REVIEWING -> APPROVED -> COMPLETE. Human as PM, Hermes Agent as Reviewer, OpenCode as Coder.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Validate workflow engine with real project. Identify Coder bug patterns and Reviewer effectiveness.

items.title: 4.1 Workflow Execution
items.text:
7 state transitions across 3 Coder iterations:

Transition Duration Result INIT -> PLANNING - Session created PLANNING -> PLAN_REVIEW 41s 7-step plan written PLAN_REVIEW -> IMPLEMENTING - PM approved plan IMPLEMENTING -> VERIFYING 59s editor.html (11.8KB) VERIFYING -> REVIEWING - Skipped (no project type) REVIEWING -> IMPLEMENTING 106s REVISION: escape order broken, events unwired IMPLEMENTING -> VERIFYING 64s Revision 2 (14KB) REVIEWING -> IMPLEMENTING 24s REVISION: tokenizer indexing bug IMPLEMENTING -> VERIFYING 50s Revision 3 REVIEWING -> APPROVED 30s REVISION: diff truncated, events missing APPROVED -> COMPLETE - PM override approved with known bugs

items.title: 4.2 What Worked
items.text:
• Workflow engine flawless: state machine transitions correct
  • Recovery from STUCK (reviewer timeout) worked first try
  • Artifact-driven: every decision/output on disk
  • Coder produced working code each iteration (dark theme, line numbers, file open, drag-drop, language detection)

items.title: 4.3 Coder Bug Patterns (3 rounds, same classes)
items.text:
1. Syntax highlighting: HTML escaping before regex matching -> patterns for ", <, > never fired. Each rewrite attempted fix but introduced tokenizer indexing errors.
  2. Event wiring: diff truncated before addEventListener calls. Handlers written but output cut off.
  3. Keyboard shortcuts: Tab->2 spaces, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+O never in any iteration.

items.title: 4.4 PM Decision
items.text: Approved with known bugs, follow-up session planned. Correct behavior: system caught issues, documented them, PM made call.

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: PM Assistant architecture works. Reviewer consistently finds real bugs. Coder produces real (imperfect) code. Artifact trail complete. Missing: mechanism for PM to give targeted mid-loop feedback ("ignore highlighting, focus on events") vs cycling same fixes.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Session at ~/projects/text-editor/, output workspace/editor.html (14KB, HTML/CSS/JS single file). Workflow validated, bugs documented, follow-up needed.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Executed 7-state workflow with 3 Coder iterations
  • Reviewer caught 3 bug classes across revisions
  • Coder produced functional editor core each time
  • PM overrode final REVISION with known bugs documented
  • Complete artifact trail preserved

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Follow-up session for targeted fixes
  • Test editor.html in browser
  • Verify syntax highlighting, events, shortcuts

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Follow-up session with targeted feedback mechanism
  • Fix syntax highlighting escape order
  • Complete event wiring
  • Add keyboard shortcuts

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Add PM mid-loop feedback mechanism to avoid revision cycling
  • Coder output truncation needs handling (buffer limits?)
  • Syntax highlighting: escape after tokenization, not before
  • Event wiring must be in diff before truncation point

items.title: Experimenting with Hermes Agent - Part 9
items.text:
The Text Editor That Took Thirteen Turns

Date: 2026-07-21 Author: Codebot Topic: text-editor, iteration, code-review, syntax-highlighting, prototyping

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Build single-file browser text editor: load file, edit, save back. Syntax highlighting (3+ languages), line numbers, dark theme. No build tools.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Straightforward project that took 13 workflow turns and 3 revision cycles across multiple sessions.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Repeated revision cycles for same bug classes. Coder produced logic bugs then completeness bugs. Reviews caught issues not visible at runtime initially.

items.title: 4.1 Round 1: Plan
items.text:
• Detailed plan: textarea-over-pre highlighting, VS Code palette, Ctrl+S/Ctrl+O shortcuts, tab-to-spaces
  • Architecture: HTML structure, CSS layout, regex highlighters (JavaScript, Python, HTML)
  • Estimate: 500-600 lines
  • PM approved

items.title: 4.2 Round 2: Build
items.text:
• Coder produced editor.html (410 lines, full structure)
  • Looked complete, sent to review

items.title: 4.3 Round 3: Rejection 1
items.text:
• Critical bug: escapeHtml() before regex matching
  • All ", <, > already ", <, > when highlighter runs
  • String highlighting non-functional, HTML tags/attributes broken
  • Double-escaping in token replacement callback
  • Verdict: REVISION REQUESTED

items.title: 4.4 Round 4: Fix Attempt 1
items.text: • Coder produced new editor.html

items.title: 4.5 Round 5: Rejection 2
items.text:
• Second attempt smaller (272 lines, minified CSS)
  • Worse: no event listeners wired (openBtn, saveBtn, langSelect, fileInput, textarea)
  • Static HTML page, no keyboard shortcuts, no tab insertion
  • Diff truncated mid-expression at openBtn.addEventListener('click'
  • Verdict: REVISION REQUESTED

items.title: 4.6 Root Cause Analysis
items.text:
• First implementation: logic bug (highlighting order)
  • Second: completeness bug (half file missing)
  • Reviews caught subtle issues (escapeHtml ordering) and completeness (truncation)

items.title: 4.7 Final Resolution
items.text:
• Additional cycles outside these sessions eventually shipped working version
  • Lesson: 13-turn edit-a-thon for "simple" single HTML file

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: EscapeHtml before tokenization breaks all delimiter-based highlighting. Output truncation loses event wiring. Reviews essential - caught issues invisible at first glance. Minified/compact code correlates with missing functionality.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Final version shipped separately. 13 turns for nominally simple project. Reviews most valuable component.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Plan: solid architecture, textarea-over-pre technique
  • Build 1: logic bug (escape order)
  • Build 2: completeness bug (truncated, no events)
  • Reviews caught both bug classes
  • Eventually resolved in follow-up cycles

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Test final editor.html in browser
  • Verify syntax highlighting for JS, Python, HTML
  • Confirm file load/edit/save, line numbers, dark theme
  • Test keyboard shortcuts

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: • None (resolved in follow-up)

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Tokenize before escaping for delimiter-based highlighting
  • Monitor Coder output for truncation (buffer limits)
  • Reviews catch subtle logic bugs and completeness gaps
  • Compact/minified output often indicates missing functionality
  • Simple projects can require many cycles when quality gates work

items.title: Blogging Skill Evolution - Part 2
items.text:
Making a Skill for Blogging Sessions (so I Stop Having to Re-explain It)

Date: 2026-07-22 Author: Codebot Topic: skills, blogging, narrative, session-to-blog, workflow

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Create reusable skill for converting raw notes/sessions into blog posts, handling mechanical formatting while preserving editorial control.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: After converting 6 OpenCode sessions to blog posts in one day, recognized repeatable pattern: read session data, identify narrative, write in voice, review, delete session on approval. But skill tied to OpenCode sessions too narrow - most writing starts from terminal logs, notes files, or direct thoughts.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Need skill that handles output mechanics (frontmatter, filename convention, tag list, save path) regardless of source, while keeping editorial decisions (structure, angle, story) with human.

items.title: 4.1 Skill Design
items.text:
• Created from-notes-to-narrative skill
  • Source-agnostic: works with terminal logs, notes, half-formed thoughts, session data
  • Handles: frontmatter format, filename convention (YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md), existing tag list, save path
  • Editorial work stays with human: skill suggests structure/angle, human decides story

items.title: 4.2 Test Drive
items.text:
• Immediate test on capstone post: "today I made a skill for blogging sessions"
  • Workflow: draft -> review -> save
  • No friction, no overreach
  • This post written using the skill

items.title: 4.3 Deployment
items.text: • Skill live at ~/.config/opencode/skills/from-notes-to-narrative/

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Mechanical blogging tasks (formatting, dating, filing) distract from writing. Skill isolates mechanics. Source-agnostic design matches real writing origins (not just sessions).

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Skill functional, tested, deployed. Used for this post. Ready for future blogging sessions.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Designed source-agnostic blogging skill
  • Handles mechanics: frontmatter, naming, tags, paths
  • Preserves editorial control: human decides structure/angle
  • Tested and deployed to ~/.config/opencode/skills/from-notes-to-narrative/

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Use skill for next blogging sessions
  • Verify frontmatter consistency
  • Confirm tag list integration

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: • None

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Separate mechanical formatting from editorial decisions
  • Make skills source-agnostic when pattern applies broadly
  • Test skills immediately on real work
  • Deploy to user config (~/.config/opencode/skills/) for global availability

items.title: Experimenting with Hermes Agent - Part 10 (FINAL)
items.text:
Retirement: ~/.hermes deleted

Date: 2026-07-22 Author: Codebot Topic: Hermes Agent, Ollama, cleanup, config, narrative

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Investigate Hermes Agent retirement residue and clean up bidirectional stale configuration between Hermes Agent and Ollama. Widen bash history limit.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Query about Hermes Agent deletion led to discovery that Hermes Agent effectively retired but left residue: ~/.hermes/ config/skills/empty database, and Ollama config still referencing Hermes Agent integrations.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Two tools pointing at each other with stale config: Hermes Agent configured for Ollama provider (3 models), Ollama config had hermes/hermes-desktop integrations marked onboarded. Ollama launch Hermes Agent failed (interactive terminal demand, then gateway status check, exit status 127 - missing binary).

items.title: 4.1 Investigation
items.text:
• Searched for ollama-launch references: only in ~/.hermes/config.yaml
  • Hermes Agent config: Ollama provider with minimax-m3:cloud, ornith:latest, nemotron-3-super:cloud
  • Tried Ollama launch Hermes Agent: failed (interactive terminal, then exit 127)
  • Found ~/.ollama/config.json with:
  • integrations.hermes: onboarded: true
  • integrations.hermes-desktop: onboarded: true
  • last_selection: "hermes"

items.title: 4.2 Cleanup (with user approval)
items.text:
• Deleted ~/.hermes/ entirely (config, skills, empty database)
  • Edited ~/.ollama/config.json: stripped Hermes Agent and hermes-desktop blocks, dropped last_selection
  • Remaining integrations: claude, cline, codex, copilot, openclaw, OpenCode, pi, qwen

items.title: 4.3 Shell History Widening
items.text:
• Baseline: /etc/profile defaults HISTSIZE=1000, no user override
  • Added to ~/.bashrc: HISTSIZE=20000, HISTFILESIZE=20000
  • Personal shell now remembers 20,000 commands

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Retiring tool requires cleaning both directions. Integration present but failing (missing binary) pinpoints stale reference. Small QoL changes (history limit) improve daily workflow.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Hermes Agent fully removed. Ollama config clean (8 integrations, no Hermes Agent). Bash history 20x increased.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Deleted ~/.hermes/ completely
  • Removed hermes/hermes-desktop from ~/.ollama/config.json
  • Set HISTSIZE=20000, HISTFILESIZE=20000 in ~/.bashrc

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Verify Ollama launch no longer shows Hermes Agent
  • Confirm ~/.hermes/ gone
  • Test bash history retention

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: • None

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Clean up both directions when retiring integrated tools
  • "Appears but fails" is strong diagnostic for stale integrations
  • Small config changes (history) compound daily value

items.title: OpenCode Configuration Evolution - Part 1
items.text:
Agent roster for specialized model routing

Date: 2026-07-22 Author: Codebot Topic: OpenCode, config, model, routing, orchestration, workflow, PaxSenix, session

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Build agent roster in OpenCode for specialized model routing: right model for right job (thinking, coding, reviewing, vision, fast, cheap).

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Single model served all roles - compromise leaving thinking or doing half-tuned. PaxSenix provider advertised GPT-3.5 Turbo but /v1/models returned ~200 model IDs spanning every known family (suspicious).

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Provider catalog included phantom models (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus, Gemini 3.1, Nemotron 3 Ultra from one endpoint). Need to verify real models, build routing layer, and retire old Hermes-based orchestrator.

items.title: 4.1 Provider Verification
items.text:
• Fetched https://api.paxsenix.org/v1/models: ~200 model IDs
  • Tested gpt-3.5-turbo: "Not Found" (phantom)
  • Tested deepseek-v4-flash: responded correctly
  • Real model test: ask silly question, watch compliance

items.title: 4.2 Model Catalog Configuration
items.text:
• Configured provider with real base URL (/v1 matters)
  • Pulled full list, stripped fake gpt-3.5-turbo
  • Wrote ~150 models to opencode.json under provider.paxsenix.models with display names
  • Note: underlying model authenticity unverifiable externally; they respond correctly, nearly free, provide diversity

items.title: 4.3 Agent Roster Design
items.text:
7 agents in opencode.json with primary + fallback families:

Agent Role Primary Falls Back To @chat Conversation GPT-5.5 Claude Sonnet, Gemini Pro @reason Deep thinking o3 GPT-5.5, Claude Opus, Gemini Thinking @code Implementation Qwen3-Coder Claude Sonnet, GPT-5.5, DeepSeek Pro @review Code review Claude Sonnet 4.6 GPT-5.5, DeepSeek Pro @vision Image analysis GPT-4o Gemini, Qwen Omni @fast Quick answers GPT-5-mini Gemini Flash, DeepSeek Flash @cheap Throwaway drafts Gemini Flash Lite GPT-5-nano, DeepSeek Flash, GLM Flash

Invocation: @code fix this function, @review check my PR. Fallbacks mental model - next specialist on rate limit/unavailable.

items.title: 4.4 Orchestrator Rewire
items.text:
• Project Manager Assistant (state-machine workflow) invoked agents via retired Hermes Agent
  • Moved skill to OpenCode skills tree
  • Rewrote agent calls: opencode run @review, opencode run @code
  • Deleted all Hermes Agent runner traces
  • Workflow now speaks native OpenCode language

items.title: 4.5 Validation Session
items.text:
• New session pm-assistant-fix walked reworked loop end-to-end
  • Objective in, plan out, plan approved, implementation triggered
  • First coder call stalled on provider issue (routing layer only as good as endpoints)
  • Session held cleanly at that point (state machine: stopped = saved, not lost)

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Routing = never making wrong model do job it's bad at. One agent each for thinking, doing, judging, cheap work. Provider unknown quantity but architecture sound. State machine preserves work on interruption.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Agent roster configured, orchestrator rewired, validation session paused cleanly. Provider authenticity uncertain but responses functional.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Verified PaxSenix catalog: ~200 models, stripped phantom gpt-3.5-turbo
  • Configured ~150 models in opencode.json
  • Designed 7-agent roster with role-specific primaries and fallback families
  • Rewired PM Assistant from Hermes Agent to native OpenCode agents
  • Validated workflow end-to-end (paused on provider issue)

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Test each agent role with appropriate tasks
  • Monitor fallback behavior under rate limits
  • Verify PM Assistant completes full cycles

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Resume pm-assistant-fix session
  • Monitor provider model authenticity
  • Adjust roster based on real performance

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Route by role, not by model availability
  • Maintain mental fallback model (next specialist on failure)
  • State machine workflows survive interruptions
  • Provider catalog diversity enables role specialization
  • Architecture matters more than provider provenance

items.title: The LiteLLM Gateway Evolution - Part 3
items.text:
Removing Paxsenix and Rewiring to a Local LiteLLM Proxy

Date: 2026-07-22 Author: Codebot Topic: OpenCode, LiteLLM, homelab, SSL, Caddy, Podman, routing

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Remove PaxSenix provider from OpenCode configuration and rewire all agents to local LiteLLM proxy at litellm.home.arpa.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: PaxSenix was default provider across 7 OpenCode agents (chat, reason, code, review, vision, fast, cheap) with 136 models in opencode.json. User requested removal and migration to self-hosted LiteLLM gateway.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: PaxSenix removal straightforward but proxy migration introduced SSL certificate validation failure, then 502 Bad Gateway from Caddy due to LiteLLM container crash-looping from config version mismatch.

items.title: 4.1 PaxSenix Removal
items.text:
• opencode.json: deleted provider.paxsenix block, rewrote all 7 agent model keys
  • auth.json: removed API key
  • model.json: purged PaxSenix from recent-model list
  • All agents fell back to opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free (built-in free model)

items.title: 4.2 Proxy Configuration
items.text:
• Added OpenAI-compatible provider pointing to https://litellm.home.arpa/v1
  • Stored API key in auth.json
  • Immediate error: "Failed to load auth provider metadata: unable to verify the first certificate"

items.title: 4.3 SSL Certificate Resolution
items.text:
• Homelab uses self-signed internal CA
  • WSL2 mount had old homelab-ca.crt (AKI: 81:7A:0B:... vs server SKI: C8:3B:66:... - mismatch)
  • Correct CA on homelab: /etc/ssl/certs/homelab-ca.pem
  • Copied to Fedora trust store: /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/
  • Ran update-ca-trust
  • Node.js uses own CA bundle: set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS permanently in .bashrc

items.title: 4.4 502 Bad Gateway Debug
items.text:
• Caddy log: "dial tcp 127.0.0.1:4000: connect: connection refused"
  • LiteLLM Podman container crash-looping
  • systemd showed "active" (conmon wrapper alive), but podman ps empty
  • journalctl root cause: ValueError: Invalid routing_strategy: 'usage-based'. Valid: \['usage-based-routing', ...]
  • LiteLLM v1.92.0 renamed usage-based to usage-based-routing
  • Fixed: sed on /srv/appdata/litellm/config.yaml
  • Container started cleanly, registering 140+ models (kenari, NVIDIA, OpenRouter, zai, Gemini, Ollama, groq, cerebras)

items.title: 4.5 Final Configuration
items.text:
• Rebuilt OpenCode config around proxy
  • Provider section: 20 Kenari model definitions (via LiteLLM gateway)
  • All agents use :free variants to avoid burning topped-up balance
  • Stack: OpenCode -> litellm.home.arpa (Caddy TLS) -> localhost:4000 (LiteLLM) -> kenari/nvidia/openrouter

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: AKI/SKI mismatch reveals wrong CA cert before deep SSL debugging. NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS required even after update-ca-trust (Node.js doesn't read system bundle). LiteLLM version bumps break configs silently (routing_strategy rename in patch release). Container "active" in systemd != healthy (check journalctl). OpenCode requires explicit model definitions in provider config (no auto-discovery from /v1/models).

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Proxy healthy, 140+ models registered. OpenCode configured with single provider, single API key, single config. No more Paxsenix.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text:
• Removed PaxSenix from opencode.json, auth.json, model.json
  • Configured LiteLLM proxy provider
  • Resolved SSL: correct CA (homelab-ca.pem), Fedora trust store, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
  • Fixed 502: LiteLLM routing_strategy v1.92.0 rename (usage-based -> usage-based-routing)
  • Verified 140+ models registered
  • Rewired OpenCode agents to proxy with :free variants

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text:
• Test OpenCode agent responses via proxy
  • Monitor LiteLLM container stability
  • Verify :free model usage doesn't burn balance

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text:
• Resolve billing situation for non-free models
  • Monitor LiteLLM version updates for config breaks

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text:
• Check AKI/SKI before SSL debugging (openssl x509 -text comparison)
  • Always set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS on Linux for Node.js apps
  • Monitor upstream version changes for breaking config keys
  • Check journalctl on 5xx proxy errors (systemd status misleading)
  • Define models explicitly in OpenCode provider config

items.title: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS
items.text: Date: 2026-07-24 Author: Codebot Topic: homelab, NixOS, narrative, Samba, cleanup
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Reduce root partition usage by relocating XDG user directories from /home/sigit to /srv/media and configure Samba shares for Windows client access.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: The homelab root partition (/dev/sda2) was at 83% capacity (54G of 69G used). XDG user directories (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, etc.) resided in /home/sigit on the root partition. Meanwhile, /srv/media -- a separate dataset on the same disk -- had ample space and already stored media files.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Root partition space pressure required moving user data off-root. Samba does not follow symlinks outside the share path by default, so Windows clients would see dead symlink entries.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 4.1 XDG Directory Relocation
items.text: Created symlinks for nine XDG directories from $HOME to /srv/media and updated ~/.config/user-dirs.dirs so applications and file dialogs follow the new paths.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 4.2 Samba Share Configuration
items.text: Instead of enabling wide links, added explicit Samba shares for each XDG directory (desktop, documents, downloads, music, pictures, projects, public, templates, videos), all writable and restricted to user sigit. Configuration declared in modules/storage/samba.nix.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 4.3 Stale Directory Cleanup
items.text: Found a stale Videos/ (uppercase) directory alongside the intended videos/ (lowercase) in /srv/media. Grep across all .nix files revealed no NixOS tmpfiles rule creating it -- likely a manual or file manager leftover. Deleted and verified it does not return after rebuild.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Samba's default behavior rejects symlinks pointing outside the share root. The symlink approach required either wide links (security risk) or explicit shares (chosen).
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Explicit per-directory Samba shares provide Windows access without compromising share isolation. The tmpfiles + Samba configuration in NixOS makes the setup declarative and reproducible.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Root usage reduced. /srv/media absorbs user data. Windows clients can browse \homelab\pictures (and other shares) without issues. All changes managed through NixOS configuration.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text: Run sudo nixos-rebuild switch. Verify Samba shares appear on LAN. Confirm Windows clients can read/write each share. Monitor root partition usage.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: None.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text: Periodically audit /srv/media for stray directories not managed by NixOS. Consider automating XDG directory setup for new users via tmpfiles.d.
path: Freeing Up Root Moving Xdg Dirs To Srv Media On NixOS

items.title: Mem0 Memory Integration - Part 1
items.text:
Rolling My Own Mem0 Integration (Before Checking Docs)

Date: 2026-07-24 Author: Codebot Topic: Mem0, OpenCode, troubleshooting, memory

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Test Mem0 connection, diagnose why previous hermes session memories were invisible, and understand Mem0 entity scoping and API key constraints.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: The client asked to check what Mem0 knows about them. Two searches (decision type, task_learning type) returned only two results from the current session (ses_1784893629), both under user_id: sigit, app_id: sigit. The client mentioned previous Hermes Agent sessions using user_id: hermes-user.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Mem0 searches across various entity parameter combinations (hermes-user with Hermes Agent, sigit with Hermes Agent, etc.) returned only the same three memories under sigit/sigit. Direct curl calls with hermes-user also returned empty results.

items.title: 4.1 Initial Testing
items.text: Ran parallel searches for decision and task_learning memory types. Received two results from current session only.

items.title: 4.2 Entity Parameter Exploration
items.text: Tested all combinations of user_id, app_id, agent_id parameters including hermes-user, Hermes Agent, sigit variants. All returned same three memories.

items.title: 4.3 Global Scope Testing
items.text: Enabled explicit scope: global via MEM0_GLOBAL_SEARCH=false override. Still returned only three results.

items.title: 4.4 Plugin Source Code Analysis
items.text: Examined @mem0/opencode-plugin at ~/.cache/opencode/packages/@mem0/opencode-plugin/node_modules/@mem0/opencode-plugin/dist/index.js. Found resolveFilters function (line 29541) hardcodes user_id and app_id from environment variables (MEM0_USER_ID=sigit, MEM0_APP_ID=sigit), overriding explicit parameters.

items.title: 4.5 API Key Constraint Discovery
items.text: Direct curl to Mem0 API with hermes-user returned empty. The API key is project-scoped. Dashboard shows 2-year-old data because it uses web authentication (cookies/session) with org-wide visibility.

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: The @mem0/opencode-plugin injects entity filters from environment variables regardless of explicit parameters. The API key itself is project-scoped, limiting visibility to the sigit project namespace. Hermes Agent and OpenCode use different entity namespaces under the same key.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Two separate API keys needed: one for Hermes Agent (daily logs), one for OpenCode (lessons). Shell profile exports cannot hold multiple MEM0_API_KEY values simultaneously.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Create new project + API key on Mem0 dashboard for OpenCode. Options for key management: per-project opencode.json with env field, direnv for automatic switching, or org-wide API key with entity isolation via user_id/app_id routing.

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text: Create new Mem0 project for OpenCode. Configure opencode.json with new API key. Verify cross-project memory isolation works as expected.

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: Implement chosen key management strategy (direnv or per-project config). Migrate existing OpenCode memories to new project if needed.

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text: Always verify API key scope before assuming cross-project visibility. Check plugin source code for filter injection behavior. Document entity namespace conventions for each tool (Hermes Agent vs OpenCode).

items.title: The LiteLLM Gateway Evolution - Part 4
items.text:
Rename data files

Date: 2026-07-24 Author: Codebot Topic: LiteLLM, NixOS, homelab, cli, refactor, architecture, maintenance

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Rename committed data files in pkgs/litellm-cli/data/ to avoid confusion with runtime mirrors in /srv/appdata/litellm/, update all references, and document the control-plane/bridge/runtime architecture.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: The LiteLLM gateway uses two data tiers: committed (build-time source in repo, baked into Nix store) and runtime (live state in /srv/appdata/litellm/ edited by CLI tools, survives rebuilds). Both tiers used identical filenames causing ambiguity when paths appeared in systemd units or scripts.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Same filenames in different tiers with different lifecycles caused mental overhead resolving which tier a path referred to. Files: models.json, declared-models.json, router.yaml, providers-seed.json.

items.title: 4.1 Naming Scheme Design
items.text: Client proposed new names prioritizing uniqueness over semantic purity: - models.json -> models-dev.json (inventory fetched from models.dev) - declared-models.json -> models-seed.json (admin-authored seed models) - router.yaml -> router-seed.yaml (committed router config, seeded if runtime absent) - providers-seed.json unchanged (already disambiguated)

items.title: 4.2 Editability Documentation
items.text: Created table documenting editability per file: - models-dev.json: not directly editable, updated via fetch-models - models-seed.json: editable, manual edit + commit - providers-seed.json: editable, manual edit + commit - router-seed.yaml: editable, manual edit + commit

items.title: 4.3 Rename Execution
items.text: Three git mv operations. Swept all references across flake: fetch-models.sh, default.nix, litellm-config.nix, architecture README, session notes. Caught sed mangling a Nix interpolation brace during bulk edit -- reverted to explicit edits.

items.title: 4.4 Verification
items.text:
• nix-instantiate --parse on default.nix, litellm-config.nix, podman-litellm.nix: all clean
  • Grep confirmed zero old filename references
  • git diff --stat: 8 files, 16 insertions, 16 deletions, three 100%-detected renames
  • Committed as a29007f

items.title: 4.5 Architecture Documentation
items.text: Documented three-layer architecture: - pkgs/litellm-cli: control plane (inventory, policy, renderer, CLI), standalone Nix package - litellm-config.nix: NixOS bridge (systemd, activation, timers, sops), produces config.yaml - podman-litellm: runtime (serves proxy), consumes config.yaml - Bridge depends on control plane; neither is LiteLLM-agnostic

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Filename collision at tier boundary creates cognitive load. Semantic purity less valuable than uniqueness when lifecycles differ.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Renaming resolves ambiguity. Architecture walkthrough confirmed design soundness and established shared vocabulary.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Files renamed with -dev/-seed suffixes. All references updated. Architecture layers documented. Commit a29007f.

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text: Run nixos-rebuild switch. Verify CLI tools operate on correct files. Confirm runtime seeding works.

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: None.

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text: Prefer git mv + explicit edits over bulk sed for renames. Make editability/owner explicit in data file documentation. Conduct architecture walkthroughs during refactors -- cheap and valuable.

items.title: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted
items.text:
and What's Actually Going On

Date: 2026-07-24 Author: Codebot Topic: SSL, troubleshooting, NixOS, Caddy, homelab
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Diagnose and fix self-signed certificate trust failures for *.home.arpa services behind Caddy reverse proxy.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Adding new services to homelab triggered browser "Your connection is not private" errors. Wildcard certificate (*.home.arpa) signed by Homelab Internal CA, Caddy in front. Certificate on disk correct, CA correct, but Chrome rejected: "This server could not prove that it is homelab.home.arpa."
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Two-layer issue: (1) Caddy serving stale certificate without new SAN entries, (2) Certificate chain broken server-side (AKI/SKI mismatch) not client-side.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 4.1 Layer 1: Caddy Certificate Cache
items.text:
Caddy starts once, caches certs in memory. Adding litellm.home.arpa triggered homelab-cert.service to regenerate cert with new SAN, but Caddy (running since July 18) served old cert without LiteLLM in SANs. Wildcard should cover but old cert issuer pointed to deleted CA key.

Fix: sudo systemctl reload Caddy
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 4.2 Layer 2: Broken Chain Server-Side
items.text: Served leaf cert AKI (E0:5B:7E:BB...) != Current CA SKI (81:7A:0B:8D...). Leaf signed by different (old) CA. Manual homelab-ca.service restart regenerated CA with new key, leaf re-signed on disk by new CA, but Caddy still served old leaf signed by old CA (deleted from Windows store).
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 4.3 Diagnosis Method
items.text:
Compared served vs disk certificates:

echo | openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:443 -servername litellm.home.arpa 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -sha256 -fingerprint
sudo openssl x509 -in /etc/ssl/homelab/homelab.crt -noout -sha256 -fingerprint

Different fingerprints confirmed Caddy serving stale. openssl verify on disk files said OK, served cert failed.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 4.4 Three-Part Fix
items.text:
1. homelab-cert.service now runs systemctl reload-or-restart caddy.service after cert generation
  2. homelab-ca.service deletes stale leaf, triggers homelab-cert to re-sign, then reloads Caddy
  3. Import CA into Windows certificate store (only actual client-side issue)
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 4.5 PKI Service Bootstrap Fix
items.text: RemainAfterExit=true prevented re-run on nixos-rebuild switch. Removed it for idempotency. Added install -d for directory creation independence. Added requires = ["homelab-ca.service"] on cert service.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Root cause: Caddy in-memory cache vs disk reality. Chain break from CA regeneration without leaf re-sign + Caddy reload. Browser error message misleading -- often server-side, not client trust.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Certificate lifecycle management must coordinate CA, leaf, and proxy reload atomically.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Automated Caddy reload on cert/CA changes. Fixed PKI service idempotency. Client CA import still needed.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text: Add new service, verify cert regenerates, Caddy reloads, browser trusts. Check openssl fingerprint match.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: Monitor for stale cert issues on future service additions.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text: Always compare served vs disk cert fingerprints when trust fails. Automate proxy reload in cert generation pipeline. Don't trust browser error messages -- verify chain independently.
path: Why Your Self Signed Cert Is Never Trusted

items.title: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1
items.text:
The Hostapd Hunt: When DNS Gets Lost at the Firewall

Date: 2026-07-25 Author: Codebot Topic: homelab, hostapd, NixOS, networking, firewall, troubleshooting, narrative
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Deploy WiFi access point on NixOS homelab with hostapd, dnsmasq DHCP/DNS, and NAT to internet.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Hardware: Toshiba Portege R30-C (workstation profile) with wlp2s0 WiFi and enp0s31f6 Ethernet. NixOS 26.05 with services.hostapd.radios API. Plan: hostapd for AP, dnsmasq for DHCP/DNS, NAT from 192.168.4.0/24 via enp0s31f6.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: Phone connected, got IP, WPA handshake complete, dnsmasq lease written, NAT counters incrementing, DNS queries resolved -- but phone showed "Connected, no internet." Apps failed, browser pages wouldn't load, but push notifications arrived.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4.1 Port 53 Conflict Resolution
items.text: systemd-resolved on 127.0.0.53:53 conflicted with dnsmasq on 0.0.0.0:53. Fixed with bind-interfaces + listen-address=192.168.4.1.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4.2 DNS Disabled Workaround
items.text: Removed port=0 workaround that killed DNS entirely.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4.3 Regulatory Domain
items.text: Country code unset (00), channels on passive scan. Noted but not root cause.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4.4 MTU and rp_filter Checks
items.text: MTU 1500 everywhere. rp_filter passing cleanly (71085 returns, 0 drops).
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4.5 Namespace Simulation
items.text: Created veth pair + network namespace to simulate AP client. Ping failed -- expected since veth not wlp2s0, so NAT prerouting rule (iifname wlp2s0) never marked packets.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4.6 Firewall Chain Analysis Breakthrough
items.text:
NixOS firewall has two paths: FORWARD (traffic through machine) and INPUT (traffic to machine). FORWARD chain was open:

nixos-filter-forward:
  iifname "wlp2s0" oifname "enp0s31f6" accept
  ct state related,established accept

NAT counters ticked because FORWARD worked.

But DNS queries to 192.168.4.1:53 hit INPUT chain, not FORWARD. NixOS INPUT restrictive by default: only loopback, RELATED/ESTABLISHED, SSH/HTTP/HTTPS/SMB, trustedInterfaces. DNS from wlp2s0 dropped silently.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 4.7 Fix
items.text:
Single line in firewall.nix:

networking.firewall.trustedInterfaces = [ "wlp2s0" ];

Treats all AP interface traffic as trusted -- no INPUT filtering. Dnsmasq gets all queries. Captive portal check passes.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Focused on FORWARD path (NAT) but client DNS hits INPUT chain. Restrictive INPUT default drops local service traffic from AP interface.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: NixOS firewall separation is correct for security but easy to overlook when debugging wrong chain.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Added wlp2s0 to trustedInterfaces. DNS works. Captive portal passes. Phone online.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text: Test client internet access. Verify DNS resolution from AP clients. Confirm captive portal detection.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: Document firewall chain behavior for future reference.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text: When debugging "connected, no internet" on NAT gateway, check both FORWARD and INPUT paths. Traffic to local services (DNS, DHCP, APIs) hits INPUT. NixOS trustedInterfaces is the correct integration point.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 1

items.title: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2
items.text:
WPA2-Enterprise: FreeRADIUS, PEAP, and the PEM That Wouldn't Load

Date: 2026-07-25 Author: Codebot Topic: homelab, FreeRADIUS, hostapd, NixOS, TLS, narrative, troubleshooting
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Implement WPA2-Enterprise with FreeRADIUS for per-user credentials, replacing shared PSK.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: AP working with WPA2-PSK. Desired: FreeRADIUS for EAP-PEAP authentication. Module split: freeradius.nix (daemon, EAP-PEAP, local users), hostapd.nix (AP with RADIUS auth), firewall.nix (trustedInterfaces), router.nix (NAT + IP forwarding). NixOS boundaries: services.* = daemon config, networking.* = topology, boot.kernel.sysctl.* = kernel behavior, networking.firewall.* = security policy.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: FreeRADIUS failed to start with TLS PEM format error. Phones refused to connect after TLS fix. Systemd service environment blocked first start.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 4. Work Performed
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 4.1 FreeRADIUS Configuration
items.text:
Built config derivation using pkgs.runCommand with OpenSSL:

  • Copied default raddb from FreeRADIUS package
  • Patched clients.conf for AP as RADIUS client
  • Patched mods-available/eap for default_eap_type = peap
  • Added local user (sigit / pandajangger)
  • Generated self-signed server certificates via OpenSSL at build time
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 4.2 Single BSS Constraint
items.text: Toshiba Portege wireless chipset supports only one concurrent AP. Initial dual-BSS attempt (PSK + Enterprise) failed: "Could not set interface wlp2s0-1 flags (UP): Device or resource busy". Fix: Replace PSK with Enterprise, not add alongside.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 4.3 PEM Format Fix
items.text: FreeRADIUS default EAP config expects server.pem containing BOTH private key and certificate concatenated. Had separate server.key and server.pem. Fix: cat server.key server.crt > server.pem.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 4.4 Phone Connection Failure
items.text: After PEM fix, phones rejected: older Android "invalid password", newer Android greyed connect button. FreeRADIUS crashed with same PEM error. Suspected OpenSSL 3.x PKCS#8 vs FreeRADIUS 3.2.8 linkage.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 4.5 Systemd Service State Issue
items.text: Stopped freeradius.service, ran radiusd -X manually with same config -- phone connected immediately. Killed debug, restarted systemd service -- worked. Systemd environment (capabilities, stale PID, timing race) blocked first start. Manual start cleared state.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Config was correct. Systemd service state pollution from failed starts prevented proper initialization. PEM format requirement (key+cert concatenated) was the config fix needed.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: FreeRADIUS configuration sound. Systemd service management needs clean state transitions.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: PEM concatenation fix + systemd service restart after manual verification. Single BSS replacement strategy.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text: Test WPA2-Enterprise auth with multiple devices. Verify FreeRADIUS survives reboot.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: Monitor for OpenSSL 3.x compatibility issues. Consider runtime certificate generation.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text: When service fails but manual run works, suspect systemd state pollution. Always concatenate key+cert for FreeRADIUS server.pem. Test hardware interface combinations before multi-BSS designs.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 2

items.title: OpenCode Configuration Evolution - Part 2
items.text:
Persistent context vs fresh-start problem

Date: 2026-07-25 Author: Codebot Topic: OpenCode, config, session, skills, homelab, NixOS

items.title: 1. Objective
items.text: Solve the fresh start problem in OpenCode where every new session begins with blank context.

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Every new AI coding session requires re-explaining workdir, name, preferences. Agent forgets everything next session. Three-layer persistent context solution implemented.

items.title: 3. Problem
items.text: No persistent memory across OpenCode sessions. Manual context re-establishment required each time.

items.title: 4.1 Instructions Mechanism
items.text:
OpenCode opencode.json supports instructions field pointing to markdown file. Loads as system context every session automatically. 

{
  "instructions": ["~/.config/opencode/CONTEXT.md"]
}
CONTEXT.md becomes agent persistent memory: user identity, workdir, project locations, preferences.

items.title: 4.2 Username Field
items.text: Added "username": "sigit" to opencode.json. Injects user identity into system context before first message.

items.title: 4.3 Custom Startup Skills
items.text: OpenCode skill system supports startup-context skill at ~/.config/opencode/skills/startup-context/SKILL.md. Skills load on-demand when task matches description, providing fallback when static CONTEXT.md insufficient.

items.title: 4.4 Remote Context via SSH
items.text: CONTEXT.md includes startup action: SSH into homelab and read repository files at /srv/repo/nix-lab. AGENTS.md, README.md, session files become part of agent thinking space from first token.

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: Fresh start problem solved by configuration, not magic. Three fields in opencode.json, one markdown file, one skill.

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Configuration-based persistence works. Remote context loading eliminates manual context transfer.

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Three-layer persistence: instructions file, username field, startup skill. Remote SSH context loading for homelab repo.

items.title: 8. Verification Plan
items.text: Start new OpenCode session. Verify context loads automatically. Test homelab repo access.

items.title: 9. Pending Actions
items.text: Refine CONTEXT.md content. Test startup-context skill activation.

items.title: 10. Recommendations
items.text: Use instructions field for static context. Use skills for dynamic/conditional context. Include remote repository access in startup actions.

items.title: 1. Objective

items.title: 2. Background
items.text: Part 1: FreeRADIUS running, phones connected, EAP-PEAP working. But config hardcoded in Nix store -- new user required full rebuild.

items.title: 4.1 Runtime Users File

items.title: 4.2 Password Typo Issue
items.text:
Users file overwritten, sigit missing. Restored users, reloaded. radtest local: Access-Reject. radiusd -X debug: Access-Accept. Systemd service runs as radius user with ProtectSystem=full.

Root cause: Password typo -- pandajagger in Nix config vs pandajangger in users file (rogue 'n'). Fixed typo, reloaded. Still rejected.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 3

items.title: 4.3 Reload vs Restart
items.text: FreeRADIUS SIGHUP reload silently ignores new $INCLUDE paths not in original config. systemctl reload returned OK but config not picked up. Full restart fixed instantly.

items.title: 4.4 Infrastructure Check
items.text: dnsmasq dead: inactive since 12:04:55, dependency failed. No DHCP, no IPs. Phones couldn't get lease. systemctl start dnsmasq restored it.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 3

items.title: 5. Diagnosis
items.text: FreeRADIUS reload doesn't re-read $INCLUDE files added after initial config. Infrastructure dependency (dnsmasq) failed silently, masking auth issues.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 3

items.title: 6. Preliminary Assessment
items.text: Runtime users file works but requires full restart, not reload. Always verify infrastructure services first.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 3

items.title: 7. Solution Summary
items.text: Runtime users file with $INCLUDE. Fixed password typo. Used restart not reload. Restarted dnsmasq.
path: Captive Portal and Access Point Bundle - Part 3
